text.p: Paul Reiffel shone with both bat and ball on Thursday as Australia opened up a 215-run lead over English County Championship leaders Glamorgan on the second day of their three-day match.
The seamer took the last five Glamorgan wickets for just eight runs in 46 balls as the Welsh county slumped from 218 for five to 254 all out to concede a 115-run first-innings lead.
Then he came to the rescue with the bat, making an unbeaten 35 to lift Australia from a perilous 42 for five to 100 for five at the close.

Reiffel's first spell of 10 overs, split between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, had looked innocuous enough and cost him 45 runs, but when he returned on Thursday afternoon, he was a different proposition.
He began by splitting an entertaining 40-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Gary Butcher and Anthony Cottey.
Butcher had hit five fours in reaching 23 off just 12 balls when he was caught brilliantly by Greg Blewett, one handed and above his head, at short mid-wicket.
Darren Thomas then edged Reiffel to Mark Taylor at first slip and a Colin Metson was bowled for a duck.
Cottey offered token resistance until he edged to wicketkeeper Darren Berry for 22.
Reiffel then bowled Dean Cosker to finish with five for 61 from 18.3 overs.

Aussie skipper Taylor shuffled his batting order but Michael Slater, Justin Langer and Michael Bevan, three of the contenders for the number six spot in next week's test side, all failed to take their chance.
Slater was leg before for seven and Bevan, who did not bat in the first innings, was caught behind for one.
Langer was then out in bizarre circumstances as he thick-edged a hook causing the ball to drop close to the stumps. As he tried to kick it away he instead knocked it on to his wicket.

Brendon Julian and Berry followed to leave the tourists at 42 for five inside 18 overs. But Reiffel then showed his prowess with the bat as he helped Matthew Elliott share an unbeaten stand of 58 for the sixth wicket.
The Glamorgan innings was built on a superb knock of 91 by Steve James, the country's leading first-class runscorer this summer.
